newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol plans major '97 refinery maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Sasol plans major '97 refinery maintenance.

text.p: The only major shutdown expected in South African petroleum refineries in 1997 will be at Sasol Ltd's Secunda synthetic fuels refinery.
Sasol said on Thursday the refinery would be shut for 12 days from September 1 for major maintenance work.

The fuel-from-coal producer's Natref refinery planned no major closures for maintenance, Sasol said. However, two minor shutdowns, each for 12 days, were planned for the end of January and the end of July to change catalysts in four reactors.
The total crude distillation capacity of Natref is 86,000 barrels per day (bpd) and for Secunda 150,000 bpd (crude equivalent).
Engen Ltd's Genref refinery in Durban said no major maintenance work was planned for this year but a partial shutdown was scheduled for May 1998.
It has a crude distillation capacity of 104,000 bpd.

Fuel producer Caltex said that its Calref refinery in Cape Town would not shut down in 1997 after last year's major turnaround. It planned, however, at the end of the first quarter to install another electrostatic precipitator that would remove particles larger than zero microns from emissions.

This would take emission levels down to 50 mg per cubic metre, which was well below the 120 mg limit proposed by the government. This was part of a programme to reduce noxious emissions by 80 percent by 1999.

The Royal Dutch/Shell and British Petroleum Co plc refinery (Sapref) in Durban said it planned no major shutdowns in 1997 but a major turnaround was planned over four to six weeks in August/September in 1998.
